CANONICAL_NAME.value: glibc 2.36 pthread_rwlock (nptl/pthread_rwlock_common.c): reader-preferring default and the documented writer STARVATION it permits

VERSION.value: glibc tag glibc-2.36: nptl/pthread_rwlock_common.c, nptl/pthread_rwlock_wrlock.c (source); Debian bookworm libc6 2.36 (the running library)

value.lineage: POSIX read-write locks as glibc implements them: the default kind PTHREAD_RWLOCK_PREFER_READER_NP lets a continuous stream of readers hold a writer off indefinitely -- documented in pthread_rwlockattr_setkind_np(3) ('may result in writer starvation') and in glibc bug reports; the alternative kind PREFER_WRITER_NONRECURSIVE_NP is the corrected behaviour the caller must opt into. Preserved: the 2.36 source of the lock (the machinery), and a harness that drives Debian's glibc (the same version) under reader pressure with both kinds. The lock is not modified.

value.built_to: let many readers share a structure while excluding writers, with a policy choice the standard leaves to the implementation
value.pressure: continuous reader arrivals; a writer whose progress is not guaranteed by the default policy
value.success_means: readers proceed concurrently; a writer eventually acquires -- 'eventually' being the documented weakness

value.failure_condition: writer starvation: updates never land while readers keep arriving

organs.human_interpretation: the single-writer-multiple-readers lock: which phase the lock is in and who is present
organs.mechanism: one 32-bit word packs four fields -- a write-phase bit, a primary-writer bit, a readers-waiting bit and a reader count -- and every state change of the lock is one atomic read-modify-write on that word (fetch_add for readers, fetch_or for the writer bit, CAS for phase transfers), so the eight legal lock states are eight value classes of one integer
organs.input: atomic RMW requests from reader/writer paths
organs.output: the new word value (the caller reads its own success from the returned bits)
organs.state: 32-bit word: WP bit, WL bit, RW bit, R = count << 3
organs.update: fetch_add(1<<3) register reader; fetch_or(WL) elect writer; CAS to flip WP on hand-over; CAS to set RW
organs.interface: the word is the lock; every other mechanism here reads or RMWs it
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the whole lock's correctness rests on all transitions being single RMWs on one word; splitting the fields would need a second synchronisation
organs.failure_landscape: reader-count overflow (guarded, see child); ABA on RW is declared harmless in the comment
organs.decomposability: the four fields are not separable without a second lock (the comment argues this)
organs.composability: any mechanism that can express its states as bit classes of one word
organs.human_prior: named by glibc's own comment (state table #1-#8)
organs.observability: the word is readable from a debugger/probe; no API exposes it
organs.intervention_readiness: freeze/corrupt possible by patching the source; not tried
organs.confidence: HIGH that the word exists and is the sole lock state; MEDIUM on the exact transition set (tails unread)
organs.source_boundary: struct field __readers + all atomic ops on it

organs.mechanism: after registering, if the count field is at its limit, CAS the count back down and report EAGAIN; the undo is a CAS not a fetch_add because the undoing thread might be the last reader and then owes a hand-over
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: bounds a field that would otherwise wrap into the flag bits

organs.human_interpretation: acquiring a read lock costs one atomic add when other readers hold it
organs.mechanism: a reader increments the count FIRST, unconditionally, and only then looks at the phase bit of the value it got back; if the lock was in a read phase it is already in, otherwise it is registered-but-waiting and must wait for hand-over or start a read phase itself if no primary writer exists
assumptions: registering before checking is safe because the count is part of the same word the writer inspects
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: read-mostly workloads are the declared design target; this is why reader preference is the default
organs.failure_landscape: a registered-waiting reader prolongs the read phase for a writer -- the starvation mechanism when readers are preferred

organs.human_interpretation: only one of the concurrent writers becomes THE writer; others wait
organs.mechanism: every arriving writer does fetch_or of one bit; the one that saw the bit clear is the primary writer, the rest register as waiting writers (count in a second word) and loop: retry the CAS when the bit clears, or accept a direct hand-over token
organs.state: WL bit in the phase word; __writers count
assumptions: one bit suffices because the count of writers lives elsewhere
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: serialises writers without a mutex; uncontended write is one RMW
organs.failure_landscape: writer-writer contention is 'somewhat more costly' (comment) because the exact writer count is tracked

organs.human_interpretation: the last reader hands the lock to the waiting writer; a releasing writer hands it to the waiting readers
organs.mechanism: the thread that flips the phase bit also, as a SEPARATE later step, writes the new phase into a dedicated wait word and wakes everyone blocked on it; every waiter is obliged to block on that word rather than spin on the state word, so that one final store by the hander-over is guaranteed to free all of them -- which is what makes it safe to destroy the lock the moment nobody holds it
organs.output: a phase flip plus a wake of all waiters of the other class
organs.update: CAS phase bit on the state word, then exchange on the wait word, then futex_wake(INT_MAX) if USED was set
assumptions: waiters never take the spin shortcut (a discipline, enforced by code shape not by the hardware)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: POSIX allows destroying a lock as soon as nobody holds it; without the two-step hand-over a pending wake could touch freed memory
organs.failure_landscape: a waiter that spins on the state word instead of the wait word breaks destruction safety (comment names this)
organs.confidence: HIGH on the mechanism; MEDIUM on completeness (wrunlock body unread)

organs.human_interpretation: a releasing writer passes the lock straight to a waiting writer, bypassing readers, when writers are preferred
organs.mechanism: if registered waiting writers exist, the primary writer CASes a hand-over bit into the writers word instead of clearing its ownership bit; a registered waiter that clears the hand-over bit by CAS becomes primary without the phase ever leaving write; the last waiter to give up while the bit is set must take ownership
organs.output: ownership transferred without a phase change
organs.update: CAS set by releaser; CAS clear by taker
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: fast writer-to-writer transfer; readers cannot slip in between writers
organs.failure_landscape: a cancelling waiter must check the bit or the token is lost (comment)
organs.confidence: MEDIUM (take side read; give side in unread wrunlock)

organs.human_interpretation: new readers wait behind a waiting writer instead of joining the current read phase
organs.mechanism: when a reader arrives during a read phase and sees that a primary writer is already waiting, it does NOT register in the count; it sets a waiting flag and blocks on the state word until the flag clears (the writer got in, or gave up); so the read phase can drain and the writer's turn comes; only active when the policy flag disallows recursive readers, because a recursive reader waiting behind a writer that waits for that same reader would deadlock
organs.input: reader arrival while WL set and WP clear and R>0
organs.output: the reader blocks without extending the phase
organs.update: CAS set RW; futex wait on the state word; cleared by whoever changes state out of #4a
assumptions: no recursive read acquisition (declared by the kind flag)
the writer eventually gets the phase
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: THIS is the anti-starvation machinery: Techne's run shows writer throughput 0.3/s -> 1.65e6/s when the flag enables it (8 readers)
organs.failure_landscape: with recursive readers it deadlocks (hence opt-in); readers now wait behind writers -- the pressure moves, it does not vanish (reader acquisitions fell 21e6 -> 2.3e6 in the same run)
organs.ablation: Techne's harness IS the switch ablation (kind flag on/off), executed by Techne; not yet varied by Nyx
organs.confidence: HIGH that the gate exists and is the flag-dependent path; the throughput numbers are Techne's, one machine, 2 repeats

organs.human_interpretation: skip the wake syscall when nobody is asleep
organs.mechanism: a wait word has three states -- cannot block, can block, someone may be blocked; a thread about to sleep CASes the third state in; a waker only issues the system call if it sees that state; several sleepers share one flag so the waker must assume more remain
organs.update: CAS before sleep; test-and-clear on wake
assumptions: a lost wake is impossible because the flag is set under the same conditions that make sleeping possible
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: avoids a syscall on every release in the uncontended case
organs.failure_landscape: spurious wakes are accepted; the comment says the same scheme is in pthread_mutex_lock (an ancestry pointer inside glibc)

organs.mechanism: compare the recorded owner id with the calling thread's id before acquiring; equal means the caller already holds it as writer, report an error instead of blocking forever
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: turns one class of hang into an error code
organs.confidence: HIGH (read); LOW on whether it matters behaviourally -- never exercised by the harness

pressures.condition: one shared resource; two classes of users; the numerous class can share it among themselves, the rare class needs it alone; the numerous class re-arrives continuously
pressures.resource_or_constraint: exclusive access for the rare class
pressures.failure_condition: the rare class never obtains access while the numerous class keeps arriving
pressures.world_punishes: updates that never land; unbounded wait for the rare class
pressures.world_rewards: the numerous class if admitted freely (throughput), the rare class if admitted at all
pressures.observable_consequence: Techne run: 8 continuous readers, 3 s: writer got in ONCE under the default policy
pressures.vacuity_condition: no writer, or readers that pause
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: make everyone exclusive (kills the reader throughput the lock exists for)
pressures.cheat_control: measure BOTH classes' acquisition counts, not writer alone (the same run shows reader acquisitions fall 9x when writers are preferred)
pressures.cost_class: throughput of the dominant class traded for progress of the rare class
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: let many threads read a structure concurrently while writers update it safely
